substantive_reconstruction.trace_and_hermiticity: For real x, rho is Hermitian and tr rho=(1-x)+(x/d^2)d^2=1 for any positive d. With P=Phi,Q=I-P, rho=aP+bQ, a=1-x+x/d^2,b=x/d^2. This decomposition makes the positivity question spectral, but a coefficient only imposes a positivity constraint if its projector has nonzero rank.
substantive_reconstruction.nontrivial_dimension: For d>=2, rank P=1,rank Q=d^2-1>0. Positivity is equivalent to a,b>=0, giving0<=x<=L=d^2/(d^2-1). For x<0, |1,2> is a unit vector orthogonal to Phi_d with expectation b<0. For x>L the unit Phi_d vector has expectation a<0. Conversely nonnegative coefficients make the operator PSD. x0 gives Phi,rank1; xL gives(I-Phi)/(d^2-1),rank d^2-1. Values1<x<=L are valid and must not be discarded by a convex-mixture-only argument.
substantive_reconstruction.degeneracy_and_d1: At x=1 the two labeled sectors have the same numerical eigenvalue1/d^2, whose combined multiplicity is d^2; the candidate explicitly says its two coefficients need not be distinct. At d=1, P=I,Q=0,a=1 and b=x is merely a coefficient on zero. The sole actual eigenvalue is1 for every real x, so all R is the valid parameter set and there are no two finite tight endpoints. No eigenvector exists in a zero-rank sector. d0 has only a zero operator with trace0 and cannot instantiate Phi or the formula.
substantive_reconstruction.scope_boundary: These are exact density positivity statements only. They do not classify entanglement/PPT or prove a depolarizing implementation. Nonzero-sector spectral constraints and the trivial one-dimensional branch are independent of any source's shorthand parameter range.
